Achashverosh and the kingdom of Paras

title.en: The added lights of Purim Meshulash

summary.en: The Mashgiach opens by saying that Purim Meshulash carries added holy lights, and speaks of all Jews gathered together as one.

title.en: Bisya and Moshe, Esther and Mordechai

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Bisya, Pharaoh's daughter, who raised Moshe, and brings from the mekubalim that Esther was a gilgul of Bisya and Mordechai a gilgul of Moshe. He mentions the halachos forgotten when Moshe passed away, and ties the theme to Pesach.

title.en: From Purim to Pesach; the mazal of Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that the time between Purim and Pesach is the preparation for Pesach. He speaks of Moshe's passing in Adar and of the mazal of Adar, the fish, whose root is very high and which the sea covers, and says that now is a time of teshuvah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: The revealed and hidden meaning of the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Megillah has a revealed meaning, the historical story of Achashverosh king of Persia, and a hidden meaning, in which 'the king' refers to the Ribono shel Olam, as the Midrash says. In the future the hidden meaning will be revealed to all.

title.en: Shiloh and Yerushalayim, Yosef and Yehuda

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the kedusha of Shiloh, where kodshim kalim were eaten anywhere in view, with Yerushalayim, bounded by its wall, and speaks of the rift between Yosef and Yehuda. He brings 'Ephraim will not envy Yehuda' and 'until Shiloh comes' about their future joining, and says that Purim makes no partition between one Jew and another.

title.en: Yaakov prepares his children for galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that Yaakov went to learn in the beis medrash before going into galus, because he knew his children would be in exile and needed to be strengthened there. He then speaks of the life of the soul in the Purim seudah.

title.en: Torah in galus and the hidden Name in the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Yaakov going down to Mitzrayim and leaving an imprint of Torah for Jews in exile. He explains that the Megillah reveals the concealment: Hashem's name is not written in it, yet it appears in the first and last letters of words. He speaks of renewal that keeps Torah fresh through the generations, and of Shimi, from whom Mordechai came.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: New klipos, and Achashverosh's reckoning

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the greater concealment of the second Adar and says one must strengthen oneself, since the yetzer hara keeps renewing itself with new klipos, even through electronic devices. He then brings that Achashverosh made his feast because he calculated that the seventy years had ended and the Beis Hamikdash had not been rebuilt.

title.en: Shushan Purim and the honor of Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that walled cities are counted from the days of Yehoshua bin Nun, not from Achashverosh's time, for the honor of Eretz Yisrael, and that Shushan Purim was set apart to bring honor to Yerushalayim. He mentions a group of bochurim who came to the seudah.

title.en: Coming to Yerushalayim; Parshandasa

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the group from America that came to Yerushalayim for Shushan Purim, and of people who borrowed and worked to gather money to come. He then speaks of Parshandasa, the first of Haman's ten sons, as standing against the holiness of the Kodesh HaKodashim.

title.en: Kesser, and the honor of Heaven, David and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that Achashverosh's feast gave strength to the klipah of Parshandasa, and speaks of the kedusha of Kesser. He says Moshiach comes only when Jews seek the honor of Heaven, the honor of David and the honor of Yerushalayim, and that the present hours are like the sealing at Neilah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Yisrael is holy like terumah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the passuk that Yisrael is holy to Hashem, the first of His harvest, and that all who devour it are guilty: Jews are like terumah and cannot be destroyed. He contrasts this with those who sought to uproot the Jews, such as Amalek.

title.en: Kesser of kedusha and of klipah

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to Parshandasa and speaks of Kesser on the side of kedusha and on the side of klipah, and of the gallows fifty amos high. He speaks of the future, when the whole klipah will be nullified.

title.en: The Megillah from the world of tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that the Megillah comes from the world of tikkun, and brings the Gemara that Esther was said with ruach hakodesh, with the proofs of Rav Yosef and Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak. He also speaks of the four non-kosher animals as the four kingdoms.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Purim and Yom Kippur: the last moments of Neilah

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Neilah, the highest kedusha of Yom Kippur, and brings that Yom Kippurim is 'like Purim', so that Purim stands higher still. He says the present moments are like the last moments of teshuvah, when all Jews gather together.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Achashverosh, Paras and Madai

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Achashverosh became king on his own, and the Gemara that the kingship passed between Paras and Madai. He brings the Chasam Sofer on Achashverosh's father, and asks why the Megillah tells these historical details at all.

title.en: The kingdom of Paras and the galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the kingdom of Paras as part of the galus of the Jews, and says the message of the Megillah is not only for its own time but for all generations.

title.en: Zemiros, and the miracle through the king of Paras

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of singing zemiros at a Rebbe's table, where one sings and the others repeat after him. He closes this part by saying that the miracle of the Megillah came about through the king of Paras, which is Iran.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Haman's charge and the unity of all Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Haman charged that the Jews were not careful in mitzvos and were divided. He explains that Purim binds all Jews together, great and small, tzaddik and rasha, and brings a saying of the Vizhnitzer Rebbe that in Heaven every Jew counts as a Jew.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Shaul, David, Yonasan and Boaz

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Shaul and David, and of what Yonasan said about David. He also speaks of Boaz, whose whole life led up to the day he married Rus.

title.en: Esther as a tikkun for Shaul; the siyum of the Megillah

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of Shaul's jealousy of David's kingship and of the moon's complaint, and says Esther came as a tikkun for Shaul. He then speaks of the Megillah reading, mishloach manos and matanos la'evyonim as a kind of siyum, and of the end of Gemara Megillah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Judgment as chesed; Pharaoh's astrologers

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that the judgments of Heaven are in truth chesed, and speaks of the circle dance of the tzaddikim. He brings that Pharaoh's astrologers saw that Israel's redeemer would be struck through water, and speaks of the mazal of Adar.

title.en: The hidden letters, Haman, and Reb Yosef Chaim

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the first and last letters of words in the Megillah, brings the Maharal on Haman, and tells of Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld.

title.en: Closing words toward Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach closes the seudah with a few words looking ahead to Pesach.

title.en: Closing

summary.en: The end of the recording.

catalogTitle: בר מצוה: Sefirah Bar Mitzva ENGLISH

oneLiner.en: At a bar mitzvah during Sefirah, the Mashgiach explains from the Zohar that a bar mitzvah is a chuppah of the soul, and that the boy, and everyone at his seudah, are preparing to receive the Torah as a 'new offering' to Hashem.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by noting that a bar mitzvah is a chassanah, which is not made during Sefirah, yet Hashem set this boy's birthday in this precious period. He reads the Zohar's account of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's great seudah for his son Elazar's bar mitzvah, which Rabbi Yossi ben Lakunya completed by offering his daughter as a kallah. The Mashgiach explains that a person receives nefesh at birth, ruach at bar mitzvah and neshamah at his wedding, so the bar mitzvah is a chuppah for the ruach. The boy wants to count Sefirah, which prepares a person to receive the Torah; at his bar mitzvah he gains 'ner mitzvah' and seeks 'Torah ohr', and he presents himself to Hashem as a 'mincha chadashah'. Finally the Mashgiach teaches that every Yom Tov has its food with a neshamah inside it, and that the bar mitzvah seudah carries ner mitzvah v'Torah ohr into all who eat it, before closing with brachos.

en: A bar mitzvah is a chassanah: the boy is wed to his ruach, and so a seudah is made as at a chuppah.
A person receives nefesh at birth, ruach at bar mitzvah and neshamah at his wedding if he is worthy and learns Torah.
Sefirah is a preparation to receive the Torah, a time to purify and sanctify oneself, and its hours are very precious.
At his bar mitzvah the boy is granted 'ner mitzvah', and he also seeks 'Torah ohr', which he attains by preparing himself through Sefirah.
Every Yom Tov has its own food, and the food has a neshamah that brings the Yom Tov's gift into the person who eats it properly.
The food of the bar mitzvah seudah carries ner mitzvah v'Torah ohr, and those who eat it partake of it and are helped in their Sefirah.

candidateTopics: Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Rabbi Elazar

title.en: A bar mitzvah in Sefirah; the Zohar's bar mitzvah seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that a bar mitzvah is a chassanah, not usually made in Sefirah, but Hashem set this boy's birthday now, and he cites the Avnei Nezer on how precious Sefirah's hours are. He then reads the Zohar about Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai's joyous seudah for his son Elazar's bar mitzvah, which Rabbi Yossi ben Lakunya completed with a shidduch.

title.en: Nefesh, ruach, neshamah: the bar mitzvah as a chuppah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a person receives nefesh at birth, ruach at bar mitzvah and neshamah at his wedding, so the bar mitzvah is a real chuppah for the ruach, and Rabbi Yossi's shidduch completed what was still missing. He then describes the boy's eagerness to count Sefirah, which prepares a person to purify himself and receive the Torah.

title.en: Ner mitzvah v'Torah ohr; a new offering to Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that at his bar mitzvah the boy gains 'ner mitzvah' and seeks 'Torah ohr', noting that the seudah of a bar mitzvah equals 'Torah ohr' in gematria. He then describes the bar mitzvah boy presenting himself to Hashem, like the one who completes Sefirah, as a 'mincha chadashah', clean and new.

title.en: The neshamah in the food; the bar mitzvah seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that food eaten properly feeds the neshamah, and that every Yom Tov has its food with a neshamah inside it, as matzah carries emunah. The bar mitzvah food carries ner mitzvah v'Torah ohr into everyone who eats it and prepares them for Shavuos; he closes with brachos for the boy and his family.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Purim reveals the hidden point in every Jew, even the lowest, where he is always Hashem's child and the kallah of the King, and that the last generation, the 'heel', is Hashem's special pride.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the minhag to hold the main seudah at night, connecting with Yerushalayim, and with Yaakov's sleep on the place of the Mikdash: some hasagos come only when daas is set aside, which is the meaning of 'ad delo yada'. Every Jew has a hidden point, the fortieth level, where he never sinned. Through Haman's joy he shows that even Haman held a spark of kedushah, Rav Shmuel bar Shilas. The Megillah is a personal letter written for Chushim ben Dan and for the Jews who stumbled. Purim, the tav whose foot enters the sitra achra, draws out the sparks hidden there. Klal Yisrael is the kallah whom Hashem will never send away; the generation of Esther, the heel, is His pride. He urges each Jew to write his own megillah of hidden miracles and closes with Dasan and Aviram's tikkun and a call to flee machlokes and proclaim Hashem's unity together.

en: Purim reaches the hidden point of the Jew, the fortieth level that the yetzer hara never touches, which is revealed on Yom Kippur and even more on Purim.
'Ad delo yada' means setting aside daas so that the soul can meet its root without the barrier of the body, as Yaakov received his vision in sleep.
The Megillah is both a sefer and an iggeres: for the lowest Jew it is a personal letter from Hashem telling him he is His child.
Klal Yisrael is Hashem's kallah, taken with compulsion at Sinai, and therefore can never be sent away.
The last generation, the heel of ikvisa d'meshicha, keeps its Yiddishkeit in the hardest conditions, and this is the beauty of the kallah in which Hashem takes pride first.
Today Hashem works through hidden miracles, and the Megillah teaches that nothing is mikreh: everything that happens is hashgachah.

candidateTopics: the hidden point in every Jew
the Megillah as a personal letter

title.en: Opening

summary.en: The opening of the seudah.

title.en: The night seudah and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that by halacha the main Purim seudah is by day, yet the minhag Yisrael and the tzaddikim make the main seudah at night, since tonight is the simcha of Yerushalayim and one connects with it. He begins speaking of Yaakov Avinu, who came to the place of the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: A pause in the shiur.

title.en: Yaakov's sleep and the hidden point of the soul

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why Hashem let Yaakov sleep on the place of the Mikdash, and explains that some hasagos can be reached only in sleep, when the soul is free. Every Jew has a hidden point, the nekudah shebalev, which the yetzer hara cannot reach; it is the fortieth level of the soul, revealed on Yom Kippur, and Purim stands even higher.

title.en: Ad delo yada: meeting one's root

summary.en: On Purim every Jew must meet his root, which cannot be done fully awake. The Mashgiach explains that 'ad delo yada' is not about drunkenness but about losing daas so the soul is free of the body's barrier, as in Yaakov's dream, and ties Yaakov's 'lo yadati' and the passuk about Moshe, 'lo yada ish es kevuraso', to this level.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: A pause in the shiur.

title.en: Two feasts of Esther, Yaakov and Esav

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the two parts of the Purim seudah and the two feasts of Esther: at the first Haman reached his peak while Mordechai was low; Yaakov and Esav are like two ends of one board, when one rises the other falls; at the second Haman fell and Mordechai rose. He adds that Yerushalayim, written with a yud in the Megillah, will fully receive its yud when Moshiach comes, a great comfort to the weary Jews of galus.

title.en: Parshandasa's beam and the Kodesh HaKodashim within

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that the beam Haman prepared came from the house of Parshandasa, and from there turns to the Kodesh HaKodashim hidden in every Jew: the fortieth level, a reshus hayachid known only to Hashem, where each Jew is united with Hashem as chasan and kallah, as Shir HaShirim is called kodesh kodashim.

title.en: Haman's joy and the spark within him

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how a rasha like Haman could feel simcha, after Esther's feast and already when the lot fell on Adar. Following the Kedushas Levi, Esther's feast brought him close to kedushah; at the lot he sensed the spark that would come out of him, Rav Shmuel bar Shilas, whose descendants learned Torah in Bnei Brak. All of Purim is concentrated in the lot, every Jew has such a kernel that Purim reveals, and a Jew should build his whole life on Purim.

title.en: Giving without scrutiny; the mikvah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that one is not exacting about who receives Purim money, and that the Shulchan Aruch even speaks of giving to non-Jews, since a hidden spark may later come out of them as Jews, as with Haman. He brings Reb Yosef Chaim Sonnenfeld's words about the mikvah: if it can make a goy a Jew, it can surely make a Jew a better Jew; so Purim can make a Jew a better Jew, and a Jew rejoices in the holy spark within him.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: A pause in the shiur.

title.en: Yom tov comes from Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that the yamim tovim come only from Eretz Yisrael, since the sanctification of the months depends on the Jews living there, and that there has therefore always been a settlement of Jews in the Land. He speaks of decrees that sought to stop Jews from keeping yom tov.

title.en: Even in galus, the kallah of the King

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Hashem did not send the Jews into galus to cast them off: as the Gemara learns from 'lo me'astim v'lo ge'altim l'chalosam', even in galus they remain the kallah of the King. This is their assurance that they are a people even in galus, renewed as the Kohen Gadol enters the Kodesh HaKodashim.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: A pause in the shiur.

title.en: The Megillah as a letter with an address

summary.en: The Megillah is called both a sefer and an iggeres: a book carries only its author's name, but a letter carries the reader's name and address. The Mashgiach explains that Purim was made for Chushim ben Dan, of the lowest tribe, and for Jews who stumbled, who enjoyed Achashverosh's feast and bowed to the image; Purim is chizuk for the weak, and on Purim each Jew is born anew and receives Hashem's personal attention.

title.en: Bein kach uvein kach: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the machlokes whether Jews are called banim even when they do not do Hashem's will, and the Rashba who writes that the halacha follows Rabbi Meir, who learns from 'banim mashchisim' that they are. He asks why the halacha usually follows Rabbi Yehuda against Rabbi Meir, and answers that Rabbi Meir's colleagues could not reach the depth of his understanding.

title.en: In Heaven they understand Rabbi Meir

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that for practical halacha we follow Rabbi Yehuda, but whether Jews are always banim is a question for Heaven, as when a bas kol stopped the Chachamim from ruling about Shlomo HaMelech. Rabbi Meir rules on the hidden point of the Jew, the fortieth level where he never sinned and never wanted to, and on Purim it is revealed that Jews are always banim.

title.en: Even the lowest soul receives the letter

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Mishnah about Korach's assembly, the Or HaChaim that even they have an aliyah, and the Gilgulei Neshamos that Dasan and Aviram returned as Eliyahu's oxen and brought a kiddush Hashem. Citing the Tanya, he explains that even the lowest soul is bound to Hashem; to the talmid chacham the Megillah is a sefer, but to the lowest Jew it is a personal letter telling him he is Hashem's child.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: A pause in the shiur.

title.en: Kisvuni l'doros and the foot of the tav

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Esther asked the Chachamim to write the Megillah for all generations, and that they agreed only once Hashem enlightened their eyes. He explains that every kedushah is a full form from alef to tav, and the foot of the tav reaches into the sitra achra to subdue it, in soul, place and time: teshuvah after pride, the edge of Eretz Yisrael, and the tosefes of Shabbos. Shavuos and Sukkos end with a tav; Pesach ends with a ches.

title.en: Pesach's ches and Purim's tav

summary.en: Pesach ends with a ches whose foot does not go out, since the Jews were then in the gates of tumah and could not risk entering the sitra achra. Purim goes in: when a Jew says 'baruch Haman', the brachah enters Haman's hidden spark and he spits out all the kedushah he swallowed. The Megillah begins with Achashverosh's feast, held on Pesach, and ends with Esther's great tav; the Mashgiach ties Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yonasan to Purim and Pesach, explains the two Purims in the Megillah, and the Purim of Yerushalayim.

title.en: Chushim and the letters of Moshiach

summary.en: After a niggun, the Mashgiach says that on Purim, as on Yom Kippur, a Jew enters his inner Kodesh HaKodashim. Every Jew may feel far, like Chushim ben Dan of the last tribe, but Chushim has the letters of Moshiach: the last generation is the one to bring Moshiach, and like Yom Kippur this is a time to make peace with Hashem.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Achashverosh's feast and the wise wife

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer: Achashverosh made his great feast to display what he had. Wealth comes from one's fathers, but a wise wife comes from Hashem, so he called Vashti to show he had that too; her refusal shamed him, and only when Esther found favor in all eyes could he show it, so he honored her and gave her all she wished up to half the kingdom, except the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Taken with compulsion, never sent away

summary.en: Klal Yisrael is the kallah of Hashem, and with Him there is no second match. One who takes a wife by force may never send her away, and Hashem gave the Torah with the mountain held over them. The Mashgiach brings the Maharal that Torah cannot be left to choice since the world depends on it, as a person moves his muscles at will but does not decide whether his heart beats; on Purim it was revealed that they had accepted willingly. A king takes pride in a queen who finds favor in all eyes, and one day all nations will see Klal Yisrael's honor.

title.en: The generation of Esther

summary.en: Purim is an eis ratzon. In ikvisa d'meshicha Klal Yisrael is called Esther, from hester panim: not the generation of the Ba'al Shem Tov or the Tannaim but of Chushim ben Dan, with small souls and a great yetzer hara. Yet when such a Jew puts on tefillin, washes negel vasser or comes to the Purim seudah, he finds favor before Hashem, who loves this generation more than all earlier ones; the Mashgiach asks Hashem that all the nations see His salvation.

title.en: Yavo hamelech v'Haman hayom

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks how Haman connects with Hashem's Name hidden in the initials of 'yavo hamelech v'Haman hayom', and answers that it is through the spark of kedushah in him, Rav Shmuel bar Shilas. Haman could not hold the kedushah of Esther's feast and lost it, while Jews who come to Esther's feast are refined and their pesoles falls away. On why Esther invited Haman, the Gemara answers that she learned from her father's house: Yaakov gave Esav a seudah, the meal for Yitzchak when Avraham passed away.

title.en: At seudas Esther: leaving with a spark

summary.en: Through that seudah Yaakov drew every spark of kedushah out of Esav, leaving him pure pesoles, and Esther learned this. The Mashgiach tells those present that they now sit at seudas Esther and should leave with a spark of kedushah while their pesoles is cut away. Hilchos Megillah end with 'tov lev mishteh tamid', so the feast should accompany them all year; at the second feast Haman lost the malchus, which is kabbalas ol malchus shamayim and deveikus.

title.en: Niggun

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: On Purim one is not exacting about Jews

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that on Purim one does not scrutinize who receives, and that even in reading 'Yehudim' in the Megillah one is not exacting. On Purim everything goes by the nekudas halev, where all Jews are equal, and every Jew has a letter in the Megillah. Haman too made no distinction among Jews, and Hashem binds them all in one bundle, like the circle dance of the tzaddikim around Hashem; a Jew should rejoice simply in being a Jew.

title.en: V'nahafoch hu: Moshe's first and last words

summary.en: The whole Megillah is v'nahafoch hu. The Mashgiach tells how the Chozeh of Lublin wrote 'or the opposite' beside each line of Reb Dovid of Lelov's seder hayom, and brings the Gemara of Mordechai stepping on Haman. Moshe's first words were 'lamah sakeh rei'echa', not to strike a Jew, and his last words 'v'atah al bamoseimo tidroch'; Moshe's life is the life of Klal Yisrael, and the last generation corresponds to 'tidroch'.

title.en: The end before the beginning

summary.en: The Midrash reads 'Achashverosh' as Hashem, to whom belong the end and the beginning. The Mashgiach asks why the end comes first, and answers from Shir HaShirim: the kallah praises the chasan from the head down, but the chasan praises the kallah from the feet up, 'mah yafu fe'amayich ba'ne'alim'. The heel is ikvisa d'meshicha, and the beauty of the kallah is that Jews keep their Yiddishkeit in such times, guarded as with shoes; Hashem takes pride first in the end of Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Chizuk for the lowest, down to the heel

summary.en: The Mashgiach links Purim with Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, through whom even the lowest find chizuk. 'Vaye'ehav hamelech es Esther' speaks of Hashem's joy in the last generation, the generation of the heel, 'ad midrach kaf regel', which will tread on Haman and wipe out Amalek.

title.en: Write your own megillah of hidden miracles

summary.en: The Megillah is a personal letter, not a history book, and Hashem's name does not appear in it. Open miracles were in Mitzrayim and at Matan Torah; today there are hidden miracles, especially in shidduchim and parnassah, and they are greater. The Mashgiach urges each listener to take a notebook, write down the events of his life and see Hashem's miracles, writing his own megillah, and brings the Chasam Sofer that a person should go through his life with his children and talmidim and show them Hashem's hashgachah.

title.en: The Ramban on mitzvos and miracles

summary.en: The Mashgiach reads from the Ramban: Hashem does not perform a sign in every generation for every rasha or denier, so He commanded mitzvos as a remembrance of the miracles of Mitzrayim. The purpose of all mitzvos, of raising the voice in tefillah and of batei knesiyos, is to declare that we believe in Hashem and are His creations; and from the great open miracles a person comes to acknowledge the hidden ones, as in the complex working of his own body.

title.en: There is no mikreh

summary.en: The Ramban writes that a person has no share in the Torah of Moshe until he believes that all that happens to us is miracles, with no nature. The Mashgiach says the Megillah teaches this: 'asher karcha' is Amalek's word, and everything, for the many and for the individual, is hashgachah. One who reads the Megillah at night does not yet see how the events connect; by its end he sees that every part belonged to the plan. 'Iggeres haPurim hazos' teaches that we have a share in the Torah of Moshe.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram and the call of Shema Yisrael

summary.en: The Mashgiach repeats a Torah he said in Yerushalayim: the Gilgulei Neshamos says Dasan and Aviram returned as the two oxen Eliyahu offered on Har HaKarmel, and when the fire came down they brought the people to cry 'Hashem hu haElokim', the start of their tikkun. Yom Kippur is the tikkun for machlokes: at Ne'ilah all souls join into one, and Shema means gathering together. Purim is like Yom Kippur, and he calls on all leaving the seudah to run from every machlokes and proclaim together Hashem Elokeinu Hashem Echad.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Niggun

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Blessings, Nishmas and singing

summary.en: The Mashgiach blesses all with life, health, blessing and peace, as at Ne'ilah, and with the complete geulah; l'chaim is said, and he asks that Nishmas be said as a preparation for every Nishmas of the year. Singing follows.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Mordechai and Esther opened gates for every generation, so that even the lowest generation, deep in the tannery of galus, can enter the King's inner court with mesiras nefesh and emunah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the descent of the generations and the Gemara's 'openings' to the Megillah: where there is no key, one breaks the door. Mordechai, like the shemen hamishcha, is present in every generation, and so is Haman. Mordechai fasted on Pesach to transfer its joy to Purim, which Chazal kept a weekday Yom Tov with matanos l'evyonim. Haman's three plans made the victory permanent. Esther lost the Shechinah in the house of idols, yet like a king entering a tannery for his bride, Hashem comes closest in deep galus, and the Megillah teaches hashgacha pratis. Esther entered the inner court with mesiras nefesh, and at the seudah all Jews stand there. He develops Yosef and Binyamin as roots of Purim, our generation as Jews of Masechta Megillah who need love, the small vertebra and a world above understanding, and Purim wine that enters the bones, closing with longing for Yerushalayim.

en: Mordechai, like the shemen hamishcha, remains in every generation, and Haman too returns in every generation in new garments; the war against Amalek is from generation to generation.
By fasting on the first day of Pesach, Mordechai transferred the joy of Pesach to Purim.
Like a king who enters even a tannery for the sake of his bride, Hashem's love is greater in deep galus, and He comes down to the lowest generation.
For Jews there is no 'coincidence': the Megillah teaches hashgacha pratis in every step, while Amalek stands for the power of chance.
Today nothing can be achieved without mesiras nefesh, and at the Purim seudah every Jew stands in the King's inner court and may ask.
Our generation are Jews of Masechta Megillah, which opens with a leniency; they need kiruv and love, not stringency.
Purim and the Megillah belong to a world above understanding, and therefore they will remain when other Yamim Tovim are nullified.

title.en: Opening

summary.en: Opening.

title.en: The lowest generation and the gates that open

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of how the generations keep descending and how low today's generation has come. He brings the Gemara's 'openings' to the Megillah and explains that where there is no key one breaks the door: on Purim the gates to the highest places in Heaven, long closed, are opened.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: Interlude.

title.en: Mordechai and Haman in every generation

summary.en: From the shemen hamishcha in this week's parsha, which remains for all generations, the Mashgiach moves to Mordechai, alluded in 'mor dror', who is also present in every generation. Haman too returns in every generation in new garments; the war with Amalek is from generation to generation, and in the last generation Haman gathers all the forces of the sitra achra, as Mordechai's kedusha gathers all Jews.

title.en: Purim needs a serious moment

summary.en: The Mashgiach relates that Reb Shraga Feivel Mendlowitz once complained after a Purim seudah that it lacked a truly serious moment, and says Purim, a time of joy, must have one. Every Jew is now ready for an aliyah and can be freed with Mordechai's strength from the grip of Haman's vessels.

title.en: Mordechai's fast on Pesach

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings Chazal that Mordechai 'passed' the first day of Pesach in fasting, and Esther's answer to his question about eating matzah. He explains that 'he'evir' means 'transferred': the joy of Pesach that was missing above that night ('on that night the King's sleep was disturbed') was carried over to Purim, as the song of the Levi'im supplies the joy missing from a korban chatas.

title.en: A weekday Yom Tov and matanos l'evyonim

summary.en: Mordechai wanted Purim to be a full Yom Tov, but the Jews did not accept it. The Mashgiach explains that a weekday Yom Tov is needed to sustain Jews in galus, and that in place of 'yom tov' came matanos l'evyonim, the greatest simcha according to the Rambam; in the future Purim will remain and become the true Yom Tov Mordechai intended.

title.en: Haman's three thoughts

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Megillah and Chazal record that Haman's plan grew in three stages: against Mordechai alone, then against his people, then against all the Jews. Since something that happens three times becomes a chazakah, the three thoughts that were nullified made the victory over Haman permanent, a Yom Tov for all generations.

title.en: Esther in the house of idols

summary.en: When Esther reached the house of idols the Shechinah left her and she cried out. The Mashgiach asks how she could complain when even Moshe Rabbeinu would not daven inside a city full of idols, and answers with 'lo me'astim velo ge'altim' and the mashal of a king who enters even a tannery for the sake of his bride: today, in the lowest tannery of galus, Hashem comes down to us.

title.en: 'You are with me' in the valley of shadow

summary.en: In Egypt, once the makkos had broken the klipah, Moshe could go out of the city to daven; but when the bride is in the tannery the love grows stronger. From Tehillim 23 the Mashgiach shows that in the good state Dovid speaks of Hashem in third person, while in the valley of the shadow of death he says 'You are with me'.

title.en: Emunah in Shushan the capital

summary.en: Mordechai lived in Shushan, the capital of the sitra achra, unlike the Chashmonaim in Modiin while the Beis HaMikdash stood; Esther was in a palace where she had to count the days to know when Shabbos was. The chiddush of the miracle is a revelation of the Shechinah in such a place, and the great wonder today is that Jews in the deepest tannery still hold on to emunah.

title.en: Shimi, coincidence and hashgacha pratis

summary.en: When Shimi ben Gera cursed Dovid, Dovid said that Hashem had told him to curse, so deeply did he believe that no one can do harm or good without Hashem's will. The Mashgiach notes that the word 'coincidence' has no place in a Jewish dictionary, and explains Amalek's war as a war against hashgacha pratis, an attempt to cool emunah by calling everything chance.

title.en: Mordechai the son of Shimi

summary.en: Because Dovid did not have Shimi killed, Mordechai descended from him and saved the Jews; the Megillah he wrote with Esther teaches hashgacha pratis in every step, like a chain of rings. Mordechai, though from Binyamin, is called 'ish Yehudi' because he bound himself to the kingdom of Dovid, unlike his ancestor Shimi.

title.en: Esther enters the inner court

summary.en: Esther went with mesiras nefesh into the inner court, where entry meant death. The Mashgiach explains that this world is led by pshat, with Beis Din judging by what it sees, while in higher worlds there is a leading of sod, where Hashem Himself is the judge, and one whom Hashem judges comes out with merit.

title.en: The inner point of every Jew

summary.en: In his root every Jew wants to be good, as the Rambam explains with 'rotzeh ani'. The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that the decree came because the Jews bowed to the image, which was only outward; Esther, with mesiras nefesh, reached the inner court, the place of pnimiyus, and nullified the decree.

title.en: Mesiras nefesh and the open gates

summary.en: The Mashgiach relates that the Belzer Rav and the Gerrer Rebbe, the Imrei Emes, both said that today nothing can be achieved without mesiras nefesh. At the Purim seudah all Jews stand in the King's inner court, as on Yom Kippur in the Kodesh HaKodashim, and may ask: 'what is your request, and it shall be given you'. Others who entered without permission failed; Esther succeeded because she went with mesiras nefesh for Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Yosef's Shabbos and the meeting in Adar

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that the Nasi of Ephraim merited to bring his korban on Shabbos because Yosef kept Shabbos in Egypt, and a masorah linking 'bayom hashevi'i' there with the Megillah. He cites R' Tzadok HaKohen that Binyamin came to Yosef in Adar, and explains that the meeting of the upper and lower tzaddik reached its climax at the full moon.

title.en: 'I am Yosef': the first venahafoch

summary.en: When Yosef revealed himself, the feared ruler suddenly became their brother, a reversal like that of Purim. Yosef and the brothers, who had not drunk wine for twenty-two years, drank that day because their hearts sensed a great day; the Mashgiach connects this to Shushan Purim and to Mordechai with gematrios.

title.en: Five garments and Mordechai's soul with Binyamin

summary.en: The Mashgiach links the five doubled letters, the last of which is the redemption of the tzaddik, to Shushan Purim, and Yosef's gift of five garments to Binyamin to Mordechai's royal garments. 'Es Binyamin' teaches that another soul was with Binyamin, the soul of Mordechai, who like Binyamin did not bow; Yosef and Binyamin then wept over the Batei Mikdash.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: Interlude.

title.en: The goblet and the wine of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the weeping of Yosef and Binyamin and to the goblet Yosef placed in Binyamin's sack, with gematrios. The wine Jews drink on Purim is not ordinary wine but holy wine from a higher world, the 'yayin hameshumar'; Mordechai from Binyamin wages the war against Haman in every generation.

title.en: The air full of the Megillah

summary.en: The Gemara teaches that the chronicles before Achashverosh were read by themselves. The Mashgiach compares Pesach night, when the very air is full of matzah and freedom, to Purim: even after the Megillah has been put away, the air is full of Megillah.

title.en: The last generation and a simple Jew's sigh

summary.en: The last generations are the main one, the generation of Moshiach, like the tribe of Dan outside the clouds of glory, whom Amalek could attack. Each generation is measured by its own standard: the Arizal told R' Chaim Vital that in his generation he counts like a Tanna, and a simple Jew who snatches a quick Mincha and sighs is more accepted above.

title.en: The judgment above and the Maharsham

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a sick man judged in Heaven whose Torah was blown off the scale as not lishmah, until a new judge declared that in this generation Torah cannot be measured that way; he recovered and recognized the judge as the Maharsham. He then says every Jew is rooted in a mitzvah and a masechta, and asks which masechta our generation belongs to.

title.en: Jews of Masechta Megillah

summary.en: Masechta Megillah opens with a leniency for the villagers, whom Chazal allowed to read early; Masechta Sukkah, the masechta of the clouds of glory, opens with a stringency. Our generation are Jews of Masechta Megillah who need kiruv and love, soft words as for 'Beis Yaakov'. After a brachah he begins a story of the Chozeh of Lublin's talmidim.

title.en: Shabbos clothes and Vashti

summary.en: The talmidim who felt Shabbos at a Wednesday seudah came broken to the Chozeh of Lublin, who asked whether they had worn Shabbos clothes. The Mashgiach brings Chazal that Vashti made Jewish daughters work on Shabbos unclothed, and explains that Shabbos testifies that Hashem created the world, which the nations deny with theories that man came from monkeys.

title.en: Birkas haminim and the small vertebra

summary.en: The Gemara says the eighteen brachos correspond to the vertebrae of the spine, and the added brachah against the heretics to the small vertebra. The Mashgiach explains that the heretics build their theory on this small vertebra, which controls no movement, and that Vashti told the Jewish daughters they were monkeys who need neither Shabbos nor clothes; the second half of the brachah is against the kingdom that destroyed the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: A world above understanding

summary.en: The small vertebra, which seems to have no purpose, corresponds to Keser, a world that cannot be grasped, and this is why the brachah was formulated through Shmuel HaKatan. Purim and the Megillah belong to that world above daas, which is why they will remain forever and why on Purim a Jew must reach 'ad delo yada'.

title.en: Calling him a dog; the cow that kept Shabbos

summary.en: Esther feared the Shechinah left her because she had called Achashverosh a dog, and the Mashgiach asks why that should matter. He tells the story of a Jew's cow, sold to a gentile, that would not work on Shabbos until the Jew spoke into its ear; the gentile converted and became the Tanna R' Yochanan ben Torasa, who told R' Akiva that grass would grow before Moshiach comes.

title.en: The hidden spark and the wine of Purim

summary.en: A dog has no side of kedusha and can have no tikkun, so calling Achashverosh a dog would have closed off the holy spark hidden in him. The Mashgiach explains that wine has a good and a bad part, and that the joy of Purim wine brings a tikkun to hidden sparks; he connects 'mishenichnas Adar marbin b'simcha' to a spark that came out of the klipah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: Interlude.

title.en: Wine that enters the bones

summary.en: After chatzos the souls of the tzaddikim gather to sing before Hashem, and Purim still continues, bound with Yerushalayim. The Mashgiach explains that the wine of Purim, unlike other mitzvos, becomes part of a person's very bones, just as wine drunk before Tisha B'Av stays in the bones, and asks why Yosef spoke of his bones.

title.en: Yosef's bones and longing for Yerushalayim

summary.en: Yosef did not drink wine for twenty-two years out of longing for Eretz Yisroel and his family, so his bones bore witness to that longing and could be brought there. Wine in the Nine Days is a sin on the bones, while Purim wine is a mitzvah on the bones; Purim extends into the fifteenth of Yerushalayim, and the Mashgiach blesses that the wine bring longing for Yerushalayim and strength to sing all year.

title.en: A brachah for Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach blesses that all merit the guarded wine of Yerushalayim and to go up with the Jews of Yerushalayim.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: Interlude.

title.en: Closing: mesiras nefesh and the great shofar

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to Esther entering the inner court with mesiras nefesh and blesses that all merit the tekiah gedolah of the redemption; singing follows.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that everything in the world happens for the sake of the Jews, that the Megillah hides Hashem's love and the end of the galus within it, and that on Purim a Jew can reach the innermost point of his soul and bind himself to the Ribono shel Olam alone.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the upheavals of the time, the fall of rulers among the nations, and brings the Ba'al HaTurim that the fall of Yishmael is a sign of Moshiach. Through the story of a farmer who never knew whether an event was good or bad, he teaches that no one can judge what happens; the Megillah shows that everything turns around the Jews. He calls Purim a fair where one must connect to Hashem, reaching yechidah, beyond Yom Kippur. He explains the lechem hapanim as Hashem's love that no Amalek can undo, the ten sons of Haman said in one breath as the kingdoms of galus, and Vayzasa as gematria Moshiach ben Dovid. Later he speaks of Rebbi's planting on Purim, Mordechai teaching kemitzah, Eliyahu as Charvona, the hidden miracle, the wine of Purim, Yerushalayim, and closes with yechidah.

en: Everything that happens in the world, like everything in the Megillah, happens only for the sake of the Jews.
No person can know whether an event is good or bad for the Jews, because only Hashem knows the chain of causes through which He runs the world.
Purim is a fair where one must take what one can: a day to connect oneself to the Ribono shel Olam, reaching the level of yechidah, even more than on Yom Kippur.
The lechem hapanim shows Hashem's love for the Jews, a love that needs no merit and that no Amalek can nullify.
Vayzasa, the last of Haman's ten sons, has the gematria of Moshiach ben Dovid, and the Mashgiach places our generation at that last stage of the galus.
There is no open miracle in the Megillah; everything happened through natural causes, and that is its beauty.
On Purim a Jew reaches the point of yechidah, where nothing exists for him but the Ribono shel Olam and he must forget all his worries.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing at the opening of the seudah.

title.en: The last Purim in galus and the fall of rulers

summary.en: The Mashgiach says it is very likely that this is the last Purim in galus, pointing to the tsunami in Japan and the upheavals in the Arab lands. He brings the Ba'al HaTurim that the fall of Yishmael is a sign of Moshiach, and explains that a ruler falls below only when the heavenly sar of his nation has fallen above.

title.en: The farmer who did not know

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells of a farmer whose horse ran away, came back with twenty wild horses, threw his son and broke his leg, which then kept the son out of a war; each time the farmer said he did not know whether it was good. He applies this to the commentators who decide what is good or bad for the Jews.

title.en: The Megillah as a mirror of the world

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the Megillah reflects the whole world: Vashti's removal and every turn in the story happened only for the Jews, and so it is with all of history. The whole world was created for the few Jews, and no one knows Hashem's plan, as Rashi says regarding the sale of Yosef.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Purim as a fair: binding oneself to Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Purim a fair from which one should not leave without buying, and brings the Lubavitcher Rebbe that on Purim one must forget parnassah and connect to the Ribono shel Olam. He brings the Slonimer tzaddikim that Mordechai comes to every Jew who wants to be b'simcha, explains that Purim reaches yechidah more than Yom Kippur, and calls for learning and davening with all one's strength and thanking Hashem.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: The lechem hapanim and Hashem's love

summary.en: The Mashgiach contrasts the korbanos, each of which was offered to Hashem, with the lechem hapanim, which was not offered and stayed fresh by a miracle. He explains that its purpose was to show Hashem's love: the table was lifted before the olei regalim to show them that the bread stays fresh.

title.en: A love without reason that Amalek cannot undo

summary.en: The Mashgiach sets the lechem hapanim against Haman's claim that the Jews do not keep the mitzvos: the love it shows needs no merit. He brings the order of Parshas Emor, where the moadim are followed by the menorah, alluding to Chanukah, and the lechem hapanim, alluding to Purim, and concludes that no Amalek can come with claims against this love.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: A tzaddik must have a connection to his generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a tzaddik who wants to raise up his generation needs some connection to it, and must lower himself from his level to become part of it. He mentions Moshe coming down and seeing the egel, and ends with Esther's mesirus nefesh, all for Klal Yisrael.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: The ten sons of Haman in one breath

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the ten sons of Haman, with the word 'aseres', must be said in one breath. He brings the vision of the kingdoms one after another that are crushed all together, says the Megillah holds a higher Megillah that will remain, and explains the ten sons as the ten powers of the other side that fall one after another and finally together.

title.en: Vayzasa: Moshiach ben Dovid

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the generations keep descending until the last one, Vayzasa, which has the gematria of Moshiach ben Dovid, and he says this is our generation. Like Rashi's 'shortness of breath', the galus must be passed through in one breath; the long vav of Vayzasa is the long stretch of ikvesa d'meshicha the Chofetz Chaim already cried out about.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: The large vav of Vayzasa

summary.en: The Mashgiach continues with the vav of Vayzasa, which must be written large. He brings the Ba'al HaTanya that the large letters come from a higher world and hold great lights, and the Chasam Sofer's rule about them, and ends with Dan, the tribe that gathered all the camps, as the last generation that marches into the geulah.

title.en: Rebbi's planting on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Rebbi planted a sapling on Purim, though the Megillah calls Purim 'simcha u'mishteh v'yom tov'. He explains that the Jews did not accept a prohibition of melacha on Purim, only a minhag, and that a planting for simcha is permitted even so.

title.en: Planting Moshiach on Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the cheder pshat of the Megillah is a simple one and its true meaning will be known at the end. Purim is the day of Moshiach, and Rebbi planted on Purim to bring Moshiach, who is called Tzemach, like a plant. He tells of the Ba'al HaTanya's mezuzos written on the fifteenth of the month, and says that we too plant salvation with our Purim seudah.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: The treasure of the free gift

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chiddushei HaRim that the key to the treasure of matnas chinam belongs to the one who truly feels that nothing is coming to him. The salvation of Purim came from that treasure, after the Jews had sinned; Dovid HaMelech too asked as a free gift. He returns to why the Purim seudah stretches late into the night.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Mordechai teaching the laws of kemitzah

summary.en: The Mashgiach discusses the kemitzah, the kohen's handful of flour, which must fit exactly between the fingers, and explains that a kohen with full, fleshy fingers makes a proper kemitzah. Mordechai taught the laws of kemitzah to show that Jews need to eat and drink and be healthy, against Haman's view of the Jews' eating, and Chazal therefore set eating on Yom Tov.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Eliyahu as Charvona and the late seudah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Charvona is Eliyahu HaNavi, whose task among all creations is to bring good tidings, and that Purim itself is such a good tiding. He then gives a reason why the Purim seudah is held late into the night: it is meant to be eaten family by family, many families together.

title.en: How Eliyahu can teach Torah; what Mordechai knew

summary.en: The Mashgiach mentions the avodah of burning the fats at night, and brings the Chasam Sofer's question how Eliyahu can teach halacha when the Torah is not in heaven. The answer is that Eliyahu has two aspects: in heaven he is like a malach, but when he comes down and puts on his body he is a man who received the Torah from Moshe. From Eliyahu, Mordechai knew all that was done.

title.en: A miracle hidden in nature

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that the Megillah has no open miracle and everything happened naturally, which is its beauty. When Haman fell on Esther's couch, the Gemara says a malach pushed him, yet no one could see it; he brings the Kedushas Levi on the Megillah's hidden miracle and notes that every word in it stands exactly in its place.

title.en: Interlude

summary.en: An interlude.

title.en: Purim will never be nullified; the wine of Purim

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings that all the moadim will be nullified but Purim will not, and that the Megillah will then be understood entirely differently: every Jew will see only the Ribono shel Olam, not Haman or Vashti. Comparing it to an esrog bought for Sukkos, he explains that the wine a Jew drinks on Purim is not ordinary wine but the yayin hameshumar, tied to the days of Moshiach.

title.en: Shushan Purim and Yerushalayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Shushan Purim belongs to Yerushalayim, and that the main seudah is at night because one wants to connect with Yerushalayim. He brings the Blozhever Rebbe that Yerushalayim is written in Tanach without a yud and will be full with Moshiach, notes that in the Megillah it is written with a yud, and explains that Amalek stands in the way of Yerushalayim spreading out.

title.en: Yayin hameshumar and beyond Yom Kippur

summary.en: The Mashgiach says each Jew should know when he drinks that it is yayin hameshumar, which has the gematria of Esther, and that the cup of Purim goes beyond Yom Kippur, entering the innermost place like the kohen gadol, into the world of 'ad d'lo yada'. He connects this to shalosh seudos, the time when Moshe passed away and no one knew his burial place.

title.en: Yechidah: nothing exists but Hashem

summary.en: The Mashgiach recalls hearing as a bochur that on Yom Kippur every Jew must connect to the point called yechidah, where all Jewish souls merge, and says Purim reaches it even more; Esther brought yechidah down into Purim. He tells how in Lubavitch the Rebbe stopped a line of people asking for their needs on Purim, says one must forget everything since nothing exists but the Ribono shel Olam, and closes with 'Hashem echad' and the call for each person to be bound to Him.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

oneLiner.en: At a bar mitzvah, the Mashgiach explains that the bar mitzvah day is a spiritual rebirth on which Hashem invites the boy to ask, and that Klal Yisrael's life is a circle that never ends, unlike the straight line of Amalek.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the passuk in Tehillim chapter two, 'Hashem said to me, you are My son, today I have given birth to you,' which the Zohar says Dovid Hamelech said on his bar mitzvah day: the bar mitzvah is a new, spiritual birth. The passuk continues 'ask of Me,' and the Mashgiach suggests this is why people give bar mitzvah gifts: our giving awakens Hashem's giving. Through a kvittel he once found at the Kosel, he teaches that requests for spiritual things are assured, since everything is in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven. He then explains Haman's mistake about Adar: for the nations life is a line that ends, but for Klal Yisrael Adar leads into Nisan, a circle. He closes with the boy's great-grandfather, his chavrusa, whose father hosted the homeless at his Shabbos table, and blesses the boy to continue the golden chain.

en: The bar mitzvah day is a new, spiritual birth, as Dovid Hamelech said of his own bar mitzvah, 'today I have given birth to you.'
On the bar mitzvah day Hashem tells the boy to ask of Him, and the custom of giving gifts to a bar mitzvah boy awakens Hashem's own gifts.
Not every material request is granted, but one who asks Hashem for spiritual things is assured of receiving them.
For the nations life is a straight line that reaches its end, while Klal Yisrael lives in a circle in which every end leads into a new beginning.
The bar mitzvah boy is now a ring in the golden chain of his forefathers and is charged to continue it.

candidateTopics: Haman and the month of Adar

title.en: A new birth, and 'ask of Me'

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the passuk 'today I have given birth to you,' said by Dovid Hamelech on his bar mitzvah, and its continuation 'ask of Me,' which he connects to bar mitzvah gifts. Through a kvittel found at the Kosel he teaches that requests for spiritual things are always granted, and urges the boy to ask for success in Torah and fear of Heaven.

title.en: Haman's mistake: Adar leads into Nisan

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Haman rejoiced when his lot fell in Adar, the last month, and what he failed to understand. For the nations life is a line that ends, but for Klal Yisrael the calendar is a circle: Adar leads into Nisan, and Moshe Rabbeinu's passing in Adar begins a new cycle.

title.en: The great-grandfather and the golden chain

summary.en: The Mashgiach says the ancestors come down to rejoice at their offspring's simcha, and tells of the boy's great-grandfather, his chavrusa, whose father seated the homeless Jews of the East Side at his Shabbos table. He notes that the bar mitzvah falls on the last day of Adar, which leads into Nisan, and blesses the boy to continue the golden chain and bring nachas.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that Purim reveals Hashem's love for every Jew in every state, that Jewish existence is an eternal miracle, and that the Megillah lifts even the lowest souls toward the final redemption.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by explaining that Vashti's removal is the root of the miracle: Hashem saved the Jews even when they had sinned, because they remain His children. Purim is a day of love, and loving every Jew, even one not pleased with you, is the sign of loving Hashem. He links the five days of Megillah reading to five redemptions, the last being Shushan Purim in Yerushalayim and Moshiach. Mordechai was lowered in order to lift the fallen. Every Jew is rooted in the miraculous letters of the luchos, so the Jewish people exist by miracle and Purim is netzach, eternity, while Haman and Bilam limp on the foot of netzach. He speaks of Mordechai's soul davening with every Jew, of Purim's Targum reaching the lowest souls, of Esther's Purim without Haman's lot, and of Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa, and closes with a call for resolutions.

en: Purim is a day of love: Hashem showed love to the Jews even when they did not deserve a miracle, and every Jew, whatever his state, should know that Hashem loves him.
Loving every Jew, even one who is not pleased with you, is the measure of a person's love for Hashem and his connection to Purim.
The Jewish people exist by miracle, and Purim, which is netzach, shows that this existence is eternal.
On Purim Mordechai's soul joins every Jew who davens, and the seudah is a time of favor to pray for Klal Yisrael.
Purim reaches even the lowest Jewish souls, hidden in the deepest exile, and their full repair will come with Moshiach.
One should leave Purim with resolutions, accepting Torah anew and holding fast to emunah with mesiras nefesh.

title.en: Vashti's fall: the start of the miracle

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Vashti's sudden removal was the root of the miracle, coming even though the Jews had sinned by enjoying Achashverosh's feast. They remain Hashem's children in every state, Purim is a day of love, and every Jew should know that Hashem loves him.

title.en: Reading twice; loving every Jew

summary.en: He explains why the Megillah is read at night and again by day: by morning one reads Vashti's story with new understanding. Through a teaching of the Bianer Rebbe he explains that Mordechai was accepted by most of his brothers yet sought the good of all, and that loving even a Jew who is not pleased with you is the sign of loving Hashem.

title.en: Mi Kel kamocha and the shining Face

summary.en: From the Tomer Devorah he explains the first of the thirteen middos: Hashem keeps giving strength even to one who uses it against His will. Purim is the opposite of hester panim, a revealing of Hashem's Face, and that light comes only through the unity of the Jewish people.

title.en: Five days of Megillah, five redemptions

summary.en: He brings the Avnei Nezer that the five days set for reading the Megillah correspond to five redemptions, hinted in the doubled letters, the last of which is the redemption of Moshiach. Shushan Purim in Yerushalayim corresponds to that last redemption, and the Megillah read there builds a wall of fire around the city. The section ends with singing.

title.en: A salvation in hiding; Mordechai and Shlomo

summary.en: The Mashgiach says Purim is a salvation in a time of hiding, and on Purim every Jew should ask Hashem for a salvation even if he is not worthy; 'lo yeivoshu' is sung. He then asks why some of the Sanhedrin parted from Mordechai and why he was lowered, notes that the Megillah will never be set aside, and asks why Heaven defended Shlomo HaMelech, but not Mordechai, when the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah wanted to count him among those without a share in the World to Come, bringing the Zohar on Shlomo's love in Shir HaShirim.

title.en: Going down to lift the fallen

summary.en: Shir HaShirim and the Megillah both lack Hashem's name, and both are of the highest holiness. The Anshei Knesses HaGedolah wanted Shlomo to descend so that he would lift those below; Shlomo could not be cast down, so Mordechai was lowered to do it. The Megillah lifts the fallen, and after reading it every Jew feels love for Hashem.

title.en: Every Jew stands by a miracle

summary.en: After singing, he explains Esther's question to Mordechai through the Gemara on the luchos written on both sides, whose closed letters stood by a miracle. Every Jew is rooted in a letter of the luchos, so every Jew exists by miracle; he brings Rabbi Yaakov Emden that Jewish survival in exile is a greater miracle than the Exodus, and Rashi on 'Atem nitzavim'.

title.en: The Haman of Persia, then and now

summary.en: He says there is again a wicked man in Persia, today's Iran, who repeats Haman's words, and he will fall like Haman. He brings the Midrash of the lion's feast and the fox's song: the One who showed the fall of Bigsan and Seresh will show Haman's fall. On Purim one must contemplate the hidden miracles, and he prays that Hashem show His love.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Memuchan's survival and his lame foot

summary.en: The Targum says the seven advisors who saw the king's face were hanged, yet Memuchan is Haman. The Mashgiach answers that Memuchan was hanged but the rope broke, and by an accepted rule he was not hanged again; he must have broken a leg. Haman and Bilam are bound together, and Bilam was lame, so the written form of Memuchan's name hints at a blemish on his foot.

title.en: Purim is netzach

summary.en: From the Shelah he explains that each Yom Tov matches a middah and Purim is netzach. Moshe is the netzach of holiness and Bilam, and with him Haman, the netzach of impurity; their eternity is false, so both limp on the leg of netzach, while Yaakov was healed. Purim lasts forever, and he ends by praying for the downfall of today's Persia.

title.en: Rabbi Meir of Premishlan and the Butchatcher Rav

summary.en: After singing, the Mashgiach tells how Rabbi Meir of Premishlan delayed havdalah, sent a rider to the Butchatcher Rav with a question, and through his answer a harsh decree was turned aside onto the Bnei Yishmael.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Mordechai, a soul of prayer

summary.en: From the Targum on 'Ish Yehudi' he explains that Mordechai was a chassid who thanked Hashem and prayed for his people, and that his whole being was prayer. One who davens with kavanah receives Mordechai's soul; on Purim it davens with every Jew, Mordechai and Esther are present at the seudah, and now is a time of favor to daven and sing zemiros.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Turning toward Yerushalayim

summary.en: From the Targum he explains that Esther davened facing Yerushalayim, and brings the Ba'al Shem Tov that a person is where his thoughts are. At the seudah one should turn to Yerushalayim, bind oneself to the Jews there and pray for a salvation; singing follows.

title.en: Zichram lo yasuf mizar'am

summary.en: He brings the Yerushalmi and the Rambam that the Megillah will remain even in the days of Moshiach, and asks how its mitzvos, such as gifts to the poor, will be kept when there are no poor. He answers from a tzaddik who gave sweets to small children on Purim: the mitzvos will be fulfilled with the children, 'mizar'am'. Singing follows.

title.en: Binyamin's yashpeh: a true heart and mouth

summary.en: From the tzniyus of Rachel, Shaul and Esther he comes to Binyamin's stone, yashpeh, for Binyamin knew of Yosef's sale and kept silent. A heart that fears Hashem is a heart, and one without fear is no heart, as the Midrash of the lion, the donkey and the fox shows; likewise a mouth used for loshon hora is no mouth, while one who learns and davens properly has a true mouth.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Why Purim has a foreign name

summary.en: Every Yom Tov has a name in lashon hakodesh except Purim, from 'pur', because Purim was made in exile. Moshe explained the Torah in seventy languages, since sparks of Torah and of Jewish souls are hidden in them and are freed when a Jew learns; he brings the Chasam Sofer on reading the Targum and the passuk about the 'nidachim'.

title.en: Targum and the achashteranim

summary.en: Purim belongs to Targum, and the Megillah has more Targum than any book. He describes three levels: lashon hakodesh, the Targum and other languages, and lowest of all a word nobody understands, 'achashteranim'. Souls hidden in that deepest exile cannot yet be freed, but when Moshiach comes its meaning will be revealed and every Jew will reach his repair.

title.en: Yerushalayim's Megillah of Moshiach; time to wake up

summary.en: Returning to the five redemptions, he explains that in Yerushalayim the Megillah is read as the Megillah of Moshiach, as Avraham ate matzos before the Exodus. He brings the Zohar that Targum is like 'tardemah', deep sleep, from which great things come, as Chava came from Adam's sleep; at Haman's decree the Jews were asleep. He then calls out that the world is sunk in deep sleep, Moshiach is coming, and it is time to wake up, daven and learn.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Esther's Purim without a lot

summary.en: Purim comes from a lot of the highest root, yet Haman cast it, leaving a stain. Esther therefore asked for another day, Shushan Purim, set by her and not by any lot, a Purim for Yerushalayim with no connection to Haman.

title.en: Extending Purim; the Maharal's question

summary.en: He explains that the seudah stretches into the night to taste Yerushalayim's Purim and, as the Pri Tzaddik says, to draw Purim into the year like a melaveh malkah. He then brings the Maharal's question how wicked advisors could bring about the miracle, and answers that the Sanhedrin truly made the decision.

title.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa

summary.en: He tells the Midrash of the cow that would not work on Shabbos, through which its gentile owner converted and became Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa, and brings that the gentile was a gilgul of Achashverosh and the cow of Vashti. Rabbi Yochanan ben Torsa later told Rabbi Akiva that Bar Koziva was not Moshiach, saving the Jews from a crisis of faith, repairing the despair Achashverosh's feast had caused.

title.en: A soul's repair and peace among Jews

summary.en: He tells of the Spinka Rebbe, to whom a soul came seeking its repair through the Megillah, and explains that Purim is a great time of repair. As on Yom Kippur one should forgive and be a good friend to every Jew, as the Megillah's last words teach; he speaks of Purim joining Shabbos, of Eliyahu who brings peace, and of the angels singing at midnight.

title.en: A different wine; kiymu v'kiblu

summary.en: He explains that the wine of Purim is a different kind, tied to Esther's Purim without the lot and without Haman, and asks that people drink, sing a little and go home to prepare for Shabbos. He speaks of Har Sinai, saying today's acceptance of the Torah is greater still, and calls for l'chaim.

title.en: Singing

summary.en: Singing.

title.en: Leaving Purim with resolutions

summary.en: After singing, the Mashgiach closes: one should not leave Purim empty-handed but with resolutions, accepting the Torah anew with mesiras nefesh for emunah and not being drawn after those who pull away from it, at the end of the exile with its great tests. He wishes that all leave with a pure, uplifted heart and in unity, and prays for salvations for Klal Yisrael.

oneLiner.en: At the Purim seudah the Mashgiach teaches that the hidden light of Purim, the light of Keser, comes down to the lowest place, time and Jew, and reveals the hidden root of every Jew that can never be nullified.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens by describing Purim as a day of the World to Come in disguise, a time to ask Hashem for every good thing. He explains that Moshe's 'birth' in Adar is his attaining the fiftieth gate on the day of his passing, which Haman did not know. He speaks of the Keser of Purim, why Achashverosh's feast had no instruments, and Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, who begins the Megillah from the salvation. Purim reaches the last month, place and Jew and reveals the hidden root of every Jew, so even in the lowest state a Jew says Modeh Ani. He tells how Mordechai 'grabbed' Adar, how Timna's good will came out through Haman's descendants learning Torah in Bnei Brak, learns from the ben sorer u'moreh that no Jew is beyond hope, and ends with Rebbe, Antoninus and Esther's nursing.

en: Moshe Rabbeinu was 'born' in Adar in the sense that on the day of his passing he attained the fiftieth gate, a new birth; Haman, who knew only of his passing, did not know this.
Purim is the holiness of Keser all day, and unlike Yom Kippur, when a Jew must rise to Hashem, on Purim Hashem comes down to the lowest Jew.
Purim reaches the 'last' in time, place and soul: Adar, Shushan and the lowest Jew, because the hidden root of a Jew, the point of Avraham Avinu, can never be nullified.
Haman's generosity came from Timna's good will to join Avraham Avinu, a will that was finally revealed when his descendants learned Torah in Bnei Brak.
The ben sorer u'moreh, who never was and never will be, teaches that no Jew can be judged beyond hope; in any state he can do teshuvah and come close to Hashem.
Purim is a time of 'grabbing': like the tribe of Binyamin and Mordechai, a Jew should grab hold of the King, accept the yoke of Heaven and come close.
